text:
sylvie: quick heads-up — planning a region-by-region rollout for release v1.42.0. plan: US (canary 10%) -> EU (50%) -> APAC (gradual). change window 02:00-05:00 UTC.
raj: ack. are we pinning EU to v1.41.x until we hit latency SLOs?
sylvie: yes — pin EU to v1.41.9 until we confirm tail-latency < 200ms and error < 0.5% for 15m.
kevin: ops check — warm pool warmup started in us-east, target warm VMs=40, GPUs reserved=8. will post smoke numbers in a min.
deploy-bot: [deploy] queued v1.42.0 -> us-east-1 (slice=10%) by sylvie. run_id=rb-3490009999-01
ops-bot: thermal-monitor: us-east GPU temp stable, avg util=62%, headroom=38%.
kevin: smoke: 99qps sustained, p95=120ms, p99=185ms, errors=0.2% — looks clean.
maria: rolling to us: +20% now. watching request_queue_depth and OOMs.
deploy-bot: [deploy] us-east slice increased to 30% — health: passing.
sylvie: good. target is 30% for 10m then re-eval. if queue_depth > 500 or 5m error > 1% we stop and roll back.
ash: (typo) — oops, meant ashley.
nash: sorry, ignore
ash: ashley: noted, will monitor consumer backpressure metrics and alert if > 400ms tail.
raj: link to dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/releases/v1.42/metrics?slice=us-east (shortlink)
kevin: observed a small spike in KV cache misses during the initial bump — p99 token latency hit 220ms for 90s then recovered. not rising now.
sylvie: hold for 5m while we see steady numbers.
ops-bot: autoscaler: warm_pool_fill=85%, reserve_margin=10%.
kevin: 10m check: p95=115ms, p99=190ms, errors=0.3%. proceeding to EU canary (pin in place).
deploy-bot: [deploy] EU canary scheduled. note: EU is pinned to v1.41.9 via config `region_pin.eu` until manual unpin. to unpin: `infra unpin eu --release=v1.42.0`
maria: starting EU canary with traffic slice=5% (control group still on v1.41.9).
sylvie: watch for TLS handoff ERR_SSL on legacy clients — seen in earlier rollouts. rollback trigger: any increase in TLS handoff errors >= 0.7% 5m.
nash: EU canary metrics: p95=140ms, p99=270ms, TLS_handoff_err=0.1%. baseline p99 was 260ms, so ok.
nash: however, queue depth in eu-west rose to 620 briefly when we pushed the second wave. that's above our soft threshold.
sylvie: because EU is pinned, we won't wire more traffic. stop the canary bump. kevin — scale warm pool by +6 for eu-west and re-eval 10m.
kevin: scaled warm pool now. also enabled additional KV cache prefetch for EU.
ops-bot: eu-west warm_pool_fill=92% after scale.
raj: decision time: do we unpin EU now or hold? my vote: hold until 30m stable and p99 < 250ms.
maria: agree with raj. hold and monitor for 30m.
sylvie: agreed. moving on to APAC scheduling: tentative rollout starts +90m after eu-scale stabilized. APAC will have stricter pin: default to v1.41.9 for any city with legacy TLS clients.
kevin: FYI — APAC has lower reserved capacity, suggest throttling slice to 3% initial and enable burst queue guardrails.
nash: note for runbook: rollback command = `deploy rollback --scope=apac --to=v1.41.9 --force` and fallback-route = `region=us` for reads where possible.
sylvie: release-notes snippet (internal): "v1.42.0 — improved batching kernel selection, KV prefetch toggle, TLS handshake robustness. Known issue: potential p99 latency bump during cold cache in EU — mitigation steps included." link: https://docs.internal/releases/v1.42 (shortlink)
ops-bot: alert-channel created: #deploys-v1-42 (auto) and escalation rota wired.
kevin: after 18m EU hold: p95=130ms, p99=235ms, errors=0.35%, queue_depth back to 180. ready to unpin at +10m if stable.
raj: +1 to unpin when p99 < 240ms for next 10m.
sylvie: ok unpin plan: at T+40m we'll run `infra unpin eu --release=v1.42.0` and bump EU to 50% then watch for 20m. rollback trigger list in runbook: [queue_depth>800, 5m_error_rate>1.5%, TLS_handoff_err>0.7%].
maria: noted. i'll be on-call for EU and APAC window, kevin will handle warm pool ops.
nash: thumbs up :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: [deploy] scheduled APAC start in 90m with initial slice=3%. preflight checks passed for US/EU.
sylvie: thanks team — posting status in 15m. if anyone sees anything off, ping @sylvie immediately and escalate to #incidents if triggers hit.
kevin: adding a brief smoke command for faster manual rollback: `infra drain --region=apac --label=rollout-3490009999`
sylvie: perfect. closing thread for now, will append final postmortem notes after rollout complete.
